paper.title: Graph-Transformer-based Surrogate Model for Accelerated Converter Circuit Topology Design

source_search.scope: Author PDF and institutional publication record were inspected; public title/author/GitHub searches did not locate a verifiable original code release. ZeroSim's public repository does not include its GTN comparison implementation.
source_search.excluded_unrelated_repository: GiantCarl/GTSM is a solid-mechanics surrogate by different authors and is not this GTN.

retained_mechanisms: Separate multihead attention over connected neighbors and each incident minimum-basis circuit loop (paper equations 1, 2, 3).
Learned candidate-weighted summation over neighbor and loop messages (paper equation 4).
Repeated independently parameterized GTN layers with ReLU activation.
Mean pooling and the original two-hidden-layer regression head with widths 64 and 16.

An optional neighbor-only warmup API scales the published 450/700 ratio; loops_enabled is saved in state_dict. The common-budget runner uses both branches from epoch one and does not enable this optional schedule.
device_level_adaptations: Learned tokens represent complete devices; the paper used devices plus net/terminal vertices for two-terminal converters.
Terminal-pair equality channels reconstruct a device/net bipartite graph only for minimum-cycle-basis discovery. This avoids false circuit loops from a clique of devices on one shared net.
Minimum-basis loops are projected onto device tokens. Duplicate device memberships are removed, and one-device terminal ties are not loop tokens.
D/G/S/B and other terminal-pair identities enter neighbor attention through a learned per-head edge bias. External named ports enter the common device input features.
Four-terminal transistor incidence loops are topological loops, not an explicit transistor conduction model or exact enforcement of Kirchhoff laws.
Hidden size, head count and GTN layer count follow the saved common model configuration rather than the original converter setting dim=48, heads=4, layers=4, head-key-dim=6.
Only topology and design features are supplied; no real OP, OP missingness, or performance labels are input features.
Minimum-cycle-basis preprocessing uses NetworkX on CPU once per resident topology; attention, merging, optimization, and minibatch mask gathering run on the selected Torch device.
The implementation is not claimed to reproduce the original paper's converter benchmark numbers.

training_integration.batch: ResidentDataset.batches automatically gathers static gtn_loop_membership_by_device [B,N,L]; design_input must retain that field. add_resident_loop_membership is an optional explicit alternative.
training_integration.epoch: Optional: encoder.set_epoch(one_based_epoch, maximum_epochs). Not called by the common-budget comparison runner; both branches are active from epoch one.
training_integration.early_stopping: If enabling the optional warmup manually, do not count neighbor-only epochs against patience; reset best-checkpoint tracking when loop aggregation first activates.
training_integration.fallback: For standalone collated batches, full topology tensors are copied to CPU and loop masks are cached. Use resident precomputation for production training.
